hook: I read all 38,159 reviews on the $26.99 pull.

scenes.visual_prompt: Person scrolling phone with a skeptical expression, Amazon review page visible on screen
scenes.voiceover: I don't trust a hardware swap that claims to look like a $10,000 remodel, so I went through the reviews.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text graphic highlighting recurring complaint keywords pulled from review excerpts
scenes.voiceover: At this many reviews, the complaints tell you more than the star average does.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up comparison of a true matte black finish next to a shinier semi-gloss black pull under a lamp
scenes.on_screen_text: True matte. No shine under lights.
scenes.voiceover: The recurring note is that it's a true flat matte, not the semi-gloss that photographs shiny.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand touching the pull repeatedly, no visible fingerprint smudge left behind
scenes.voiceover: Reviewers say the stainless steel resists fingerprints better than brushed nickel does.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split screen comparing a chipped cheap powder-coated black pull against an intact stainless one
scenes.voiceover: The cheaper powder-coated pulls in the $15 to $20 range reportedly chip at the screws within a year, this one reviewers say holds up.

scenes.visual_prompt: Price tag graphic reading $26.99 for 30 pulls over a product shot
scenes.voiceover: All of that for 90 cents a pull.

scenes.visual_prompt: Link-in-bio card graphic over finished kitchen shot
scenes.on_screen_text: Full review breakdown, link in bio
scenes.voiceover: I laid out every complaint and every fit detail in the full post, link in bio.

caption: I don't trust hardware that claims to look like a $10K remodel without checking the reviews first. Here's what 38,159 ratings actually say about fit, finish, and durability. Full writeup linked in bio.
